title: Minimum Additions to Make Valid String
summary: Determine the least number of 'a', 'b', or 'c' insertions needed to transform a given string into a valid string by repeating 'abc'.
statement: Determine the least number of 'a', 'b', or 'c' insertions needed to transform a given string into a valid string by repeating 'abc'.
constraints: A valid final string is one or more consecutive copies of abc.
You may insert only a, b, or c without deleting or reordering word.
Return the minimum number of inserted characters.
hints: Track which character position is expected next in the repeating abc pattern.
Before each original character, insert the cyclic gap from expected to that character.
Advance expected to the character after the one retained, then fill the final partial block.
The order is fixed, so every skipped pattern position requires one insertion and greedily matching each original character as early as possible cannot hurt later matches.
editorial: The order is fixed, so every skipped pattern position requires one insertion and greedily matching each original character as early as possible cannot hurt later matches.

tests.explanation: Insert a before b and c after it to obtain abc, requiring two insertions.
Each original a must begin a separate abc block, requiring six insertions.
